- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for early horizon (1–7 days) and 20–50% for late horizon (10–30 days).  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–40% for early horizon, especially if recent prices are trending down.  
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.00), especially in 10–15 day horizon; apply a 20–30% downward correction after such spikes.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 15–30 day horizon: if forecast is >20% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 15–25% for next 10–15 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates in high-sentiment periods; apply a 25–40% downward adjustment if sentiment >0.67 for 3+ consecutive days.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and model shows high volatility, apply smoothing: reduce forecast variance by 20–30% for 10–20 day horizon.
